text:
Predicates:
Capital(x, y) ::: x is the capital of y.
Populous(x) ::: x is the most populous nation.
Location(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Host(x, y, z) ::: x hosted the y Olympics in year z.
University(x, y) ::: x has y universities.
Rank(x, y) ::: x ranks among the best y in the world.
Premises:
Capital(beijing, peoplesRepublicOfChina) ::: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
Capital(beijing, worldsMostPopulousNation) ::: Beijing is the capital city of the world's most populous nation.
Location(beijing, northernChina) ::: Beijing is located in Northern China.
Host(beijing, summer, year2008) ∧ Host(beijing, summerParalympics, year2008) ::: Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and 2008 Summer Paralympics Games.
Host(beijing, summer, year) ∧ Host(beijing, winter, year) ∧ Host(beijing, summerParalympics, year) ∧ Host(beijing, winterParalympics, year) ::: Beijing has hosted the Summer and Winter Olympics and the Summer and Winter Paralympics.
University(beijing, 91) ∧ ∀x (University(beijing, x) → Rank(x, bestUniversitiesInTheWorld)) ::: Many of Beijing's 91 universities consistently rank among the best universities in the world.
Conclusion:
Host(beijing, summer, year2008) ∧ Host(beijing, winter, year) ::: Beijing hosted both the 2008 Summer Olympics and the Winter Olympics.
